text: The Hubble tension is the statistically significant (> 5σ) discrepancy between the value of the present‑day Hubble constant, \(H_0\), inferred from early‑universe measurements (primarily the cosmic microwave background, CMB, within the ΛCDM framework) and the value obtained from late‑time, local distance‑ladder observations (e.g., Cepheid‑calibrated Type Ia supernovae). The CMB‑inferred value is about \(H_0 \simeq 67.3\) km s\(^{-1}\) Mpc\(^{-1}\) while local measurements give \(H_0 \simeq 73\) km s\(^{-1}\) Mpc\(^{-1}\) [1][2][3]. This tension persists despite high precision and has motivated extensive investigations into possible new physics or unaccounted systematics.
